From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kelsey Park <kelsey.park@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quarter kickoff: cohesion huddle for OKR owners — please review and commit

Team —

Attaching the first pass at the owner compact for the quarter (Q4_owner_compact_v1.pdf). High-level ask: read the compact, confirm owner commitments, and call out any metric gaps by EOD Monday. This is a short, leadership-facing packet — we need to lock owners and gating metrics before the org kickoff next Thursday.

Notes / context:
- Focus areas: latency/cost per token, model-version rollout plan, and the new dedicated capacity pilot gating metrics.
- Suggested owner-level targets are in the first tab of the PDF; measurement rubric is a separate file.
- Kelsey from Acme is looped in for the partner pilot alignment (they'll co-sponsor integration milestones).

As next steps:
1) Reply with ACCEPT / PROPOSE_CHANGE + 1–2 bullet rationale.
2) If PROPOSE_CHANGE, add suggested target and how you'd validate.

I'll consolidate responses and publish the signed compact by Tuesday noon.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Product & GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q4_owner_compact_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Subject: Re: Quarter kickoff: cohesion huddle for OKR owners — please review and commit

ACCEPT (with one quick question).

The latency targets on page 2 look reasonable for steady-state traffic, but we need a short sentence about how these targets shift during the Acme pilot burst windows. Specifically: what SLO should trigger autoscale vs. fall back to the lower-cost model variant? If we don't define the threshold, the SRE teams will default to conservative scaling and that will blow committed cost targets.

Suggested: add a table that maps traffic percentile -> routing policy (e.g., p95 < 250ms -> primary; p95 250–400ms -> burst pool; p95 > 400ms -> degraded model variant). Happy to draft a quick paragraph.

Marcus
Director, Serving Runtime

PROPOSE_CHANGE — measurement clarity.

I reviewed the compact and the attached draft rubric (measurement_rubric_v2.xlsx). Two suggested changes:
1) Make "quality regressions" an explicit gating signal (not just a monitoring flag). If we accept automatic model variant fallback for cost control, we must also define the evaluation prompt set and a weekly sampling cadence.
2) Add an acceptance test for the dedicated pool that includes cold-start latency and a sample throughput run at our baseline qps.

I've uploaded a short doc with the evaluation prompts and sampling cadence to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AqZk-example-drive-link (folder: Q4_owner_tests).

If folks are comfortable, I can incorporate these into the rubric and send v2 by Monday morning.

—Naomi
Head of Quality & Evals

Thanks all — summary and next steps: 

1) ACCEPTs: Grace (owns rollout checklist), Marcus (accepts but will send routing table), Karthik (see below).
2) Naomi to publish measurement rubric v2 Monday morning. Please include explicit gating signals and the prompt sample set.
3) Marcus to circulate routing thresholds by EOD Monday; Grace will integrate them into the checklist.
4) Proposed partner handoff: Wed 9/24 10:00–10:30am PT (Kelsey confirmed offline).

Karthik, can you confirm resource commitment for the dedicated pool (approx 4x A100-equivalent slots) and any scheduling constraints? If you accept, reply with ACCEPT_RESOURCE so I can include it in the signed compact.

I'll publish the consolidated compact and a short leadership one-pager on Tuesday at noon (Drive link and HS-98765 will be attached). If anything changes before then, flag it here or ping me directly.

Final note: attachments and checklist items are part of the leadership pack — we need the signed acceptance (one-line replies are fine) to meet the org kickoff timeline.

Evelyn
VP, Product & GTM
